solution: For a convex function continuous at0 with f(0)=0, convex secant slopes f(x)/x increase. But the printed hypotheses only impose f″>0 for x>0: f(0)=0 and f(x)=x²+1 for x>0 satisfy them, while g=x+1/x decreases on(0,1) and increases thereafter. Thus A needs continuity at the endpoint.

answer: D · B satisfies WARP; A does not
solution: A spends30 in each month. At the other month’s prices each chosen bundle costs25, creating a strict revealed-preference cycle. B spends30 in each month: the new bundle(4,9) would cost35 at old prices, so it was not affordable then. The old B bundle costs30 at new prices; this one-way relation creates no WARP violation.
hint: Price both bundles at both price vectors.

solution: The best-response equations are $2q_1+q_2=1-\kappa_1$ and $q_1+2q_2=1-\kappa_2$. Thus $q_2=(1-2\kappa_2+\kappa_1)/3>0$. Its first-order condition implies price−κ₂=q₂, so profit equals q₂².

solution: A numerical utility representation transfers transitivity of the numerical ≥ relation to preferences. A non-transitive relation therefore cannot have such a representation.

solution: Marginal utilities depend on the chosen cardinal representation, whereas MRS and its changes do not. For example a convex increasing transformation can change marginal-utility curvature without changing preferences. Diminishing MU in only one good also leaves cross-effects and the other good uncontrolled, so it cannot guarantee diminishing MRS.
hint: Separate an ordinal MRS property from cardinal marginal utility.
